descriptionChirho: The sacred authoritative writings, referring to the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament) and, by extension in later NT usage, to apostolic writings recognized as having divine authority. The two clusters split singular (31x: 'the Scripture') from plural (20x: 'the Scriptures'), but both denote the same referent — the inspired written word of God. Translations are perfectly parallel across languages: Spanish 'Escritura/Escrituras,' Hindi 'शास्त्र/शास्त्रों' and 'पवित्रशास्त्र/पवित्रशास्त्रों' (holy scripture/s), Arabic 'الكِتاب/كُتُب' (the Book/books — same root k-t-b), Korean '성경/성경들' (Bible/Bibles), Swahili 'Maandiko/maandiko' (writings — capitalization varies but the word is identical). Singular uses often introduce quotation formulas ('the Scripture says,' John 7:38, Gal 3:8), while plural uses reference the corpus as a whole ('searching the Scriptures,' John 5:39, Acts 17:11).
